newsitem.title: UK: Growth in UK retail sector picks up in March - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Growth in UK retail sector picks up in March - CBI.

text.p: Activity in the UK's retail sector picked up in the year to March, although the rate of increase was slightly lower than retialers expected, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Thursday.
In its March distributive sales survey, it said 49 percent of retailers reported increased sales volumes compared with the same time a year earlier, while 16 percent said it was down.
This leaves a positive balance of 33 percent reporting growth compared with 24 in February and 27 percent in March 1996.

"The better pace of retail sales growth reported in March is expected to continue in April and it is encouraging to see a wide range of sectors experiencing growth," said Kate Barker, chief economic adviser at the CBI. The CBI said the three monthly trend indicated that the slowdown in the pace of sales growth had levelled off.
Barker said the rate of increase was still below that reported in the June to November period last year and that the slightly earlier Easter might have boosted March sales.

The survey also showed wholesalers reported a slowdown in volume growth in March in line with expectations. But business was still considered to be well above average for the time of year, to the greatest extent since March 1996.
Orders placed with wholesalers' suppliers rose well above expectations in March and stock levels were reported at their highest level since August 1996.

Motor traders' volumes were lower in March despite expectations of an upturn, and sales were reported at below average for the time of year for the first time since October 1996. Orders placed with suppliers fell by the largest rate since November 1995.
